title: Fed hikes +25bps (Sep 2026) - the first increase since 2023 and its cross-thread transmission
source: Public record: FOMC statement + dot plot (16 Sep 2026); CNBC/Kiplinger/BondSavvy. Macro overlay (structural; no financial-core edges). HONESTY: the decision, vote, and dot plot = fact; the transmission effects (costlier AI debt, stablecoin-float tailwind, subprime squeeze) are directionally sound economics = fact-of-direction, with magnitude/lag = interpretation.

edges.notes: Jerome Powell chairs the Federal Reserve / FOMC that delivered the September 2026 hike (fact).

16 Sep 2026: FOMC raised the target range +25bps to 3.75-4.00% - the FIRST hike since 2023 - by a unanimous 12-0 vote (a reversal from July's 9-3 hold, when 3 members dissented FOR a hike). Cited elevated inflation (oil-price spike / war) + bond-market pressure. Dot plot: another hike possible by yearend (4.00-4.25%); 2027 split. A sharp turn from March's projected CUTS (fact).

The hike partly answered bond-market pressure - it was unusual for the funds rate to sit so far below where yields traded; higher-for-longer lifts the discount rate across the map (fact-of-direction).
Higher rates raise refinancing + discounting costs on the SINK/bond thread - tightening the screws on leveraged, negative-cash-flow borrowers (fact-of-direction; magnitude interpretive).

Directly raises the cost of the AI-datacenter debt wave: floating-rate facilities (e.g. CoreWeave's ~11% GPU-collateralized loans) reprice higher, and new SPV debt prices off higher Treasuries - squeezing the private-credit-funded buildout mapped in spec-ai-datacenter-debt-spv (fact-of-direction).

Higher financing costs pressure the debt-funded AI capex - worsening the depreciation/duration-mismatch trap (expensive GPUs financed with costlier debt against fast-obsoleting collateral) (fact-of-direction; interpretation of the trap).

A tailwind for stablecoin ISSUERS: higher T-bill yields fatten reserve income on the float (Circle/Tether/USD1/Arc/USDtb all earn the carry) - the same higher-for-longer that hurts borrowers pays the issuers (fact-of-direction).

Higher-for-longer squeezes the consumer tail - subprime auto + card delinquencies (the stress in macro-consumer-abs-subprime); the hike compounds an already-strained household-credit bottom (fact-of-direction).
